text: In the windswept market town of Astley Down, the annual Larkmere kite festival returned on Saturday to brighten a grey October sky above the old towpath fields. First held in 1987 by local schoolteacher Miriam Vale, the gathering has grown from a modest dozen handmade kites into a four-day celebration drawing nearly 8,000 visitors each year. This season’s event featured 214 entries from across the Northfold district, including the prize-winning silver eel design flown by brothers Tomas and Rian Hedd. Town clerk Joss Merrow said the festival remains “a quiet marker of community pride,” recalling that even during the wet years of 2003 and 2011, the kites were raised. In Astley Down, tradition still seems to travel on the wind.
